title: kumiko api-docs generates HTTP API docs from the registry and the PAT scopes
detail: `kumiko api-docs [--out <dir>] [--locales en,de] [--check]` reads `kumiko.config.ts` and writes `<out>/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1 with only the handlers some PAT scope reaches, one request wrapper per handler with a `type` discriminator), `<out>/<locale>/overview.md` (endpoints, body, envelopes, error codes with HTTP status, versions, lists, batches, safe retries), `<out>/<locale>/tokens.md` (create path from the app's nav labels, scope table, expiry, rate limit, errors, revoke, security, optional plan note) and `<out>/<locale>/reference/<scope>.md` (per handler: title, description, required grant, field table, curl example, recorded response), plus `<out>/index.json` with order, source versions and language independent anchor ids per heading. Output is plain GFM with only `title` and `description` in the frontmatter, so Astro and Starlight render it as is, and it is byte identical for the same input. New `AppConfig.apiDocs` options: `appName`, `baseUrl` (required), `locales`, `planNote`, `uiOnlyWrites` (pattern plus reason), `texts` (paragraph overrides per locale) and `examplesDir`. `--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when a handler in a scope has no description or no description translation (new gap kind `handlerWithoutDescriptionTranslation`, key `handlerDescriptionKey(qn)`), when a write that a screen triggers lies in no scope and is not listed in `uiOnlyWrites`, when a `uiOnlyWrites` entry matches nothing, or when the committed output differs. Known gap: the screen write check only looks at features with at least one handler in a scope. New exports: `frameworkErrorHttpStatus`, `FrameworkErrorCode`, `patAuthRejectHttpStatus`, `PAT_RATE_LIMITED_CODE`, `qnMatches`, `patAllows`, `handlerDescriptionKey`, `patScopesFromFeature`, `PAT_MAX_EXPIRES_IN_DAYS`, and `ApiExampleFileSchema` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/api-example`.

title: api-docs token guide covers client code, logs and leaks
detail: The security list in `tokens.md` now says never to keep a token in an app or web page or in a log, and to revoke a token at once if it may have leaked, in all five locales. Regenerate with `kumiko api-docs`; `--check` reports the changed `tokens.md` until then.

title: api-docs names events by wireName and skips system-only handlers
detail: `events.md` headings and anchors, the OpenAPI `webhooks` keys and their `summary` use the wire name; the contract QN stays as `x-kumiko-qn` in OpenAPI and as the anchor `qn` in `index.json`. Write and query handlers whose `access.roles` are only `["system"]` are no longer documented, even when a scope pattern such as `app:write:monitor:*` matches them, and the `uiWriteOutsideScopes` check ignores them.

title: kumiko api-docs documents webhook events
detail: When a scope lists events, the output gains `<locale>/events.md` (delivery text from `apiDocs.webhookDelivery`, versioning rules, one section per event with fields and a recorded example), an OpenAPI 3.1 `webhooks` section keyed by event name and an `events` page in `index.json`. New problems `webhookDeliveryTextMissing` and `webhookEventWithoutDescriptionTranslation`. Field descriptions come from `.describe()` on declared payloads and from the entity field translations on derived ones. `ApiDocsInput.webhookExamples` is optional; `kumiko api-docs` reads `<examplesDir>/webhooks/*.json`.

title: Agent write handlers can be marked as proposal changes
detail: AgentHandlerHints takes effect "proposal" for a write whose result is itself a suggestion that a person approves later (for example a plan step the clerk still checks). resolveAgentExposure, the agent manifest handler entry and the write ToolDispatchDescriptor carry the effect, so an agent runtime can skip its own approval step for these calls. Boot rejects effect "proposal" unless the handler declares risk "low" explicitly (the write default is mid), and rejects any effect on a query handler.

title: Agent manifest labels are one string in the requested locale
detail: `buildAgentManifest` used to emit every label in every locale (`labels: { de, en, es }`, often `{}`), although the caller names one `locale`. Entities, fields, navs and workspaces now carry `label?: string`, screens `title?: string`, picked in the requested locale, then English, then the first other locale, and left out when untranslated. Empty `params` and `workspaces` on screens, empty `workspaces` on navs and an empty handler `description` are left out as well (`description`, `params` and `workspaces` are optional in the types). `buildToolCatalog` reads the new fields.
migration: Read `entity.label`, `field.label`, `nav.label`, `workspace.label` and `screen.title` instead of the `labels`/`titles` maps. Code that only passes the manifest to `buildToolCatalog` or serialises it needs no change.

title: Agent manifest shows only the first sentence of a feature description
detail: `buildAgentManifest` emits the first sentence of `FeatureDefinition.description` (a `. ` before a capital letter ends it, so "e.g." and "Art. 15" stay whole), at most 300 characters. The full text stays on the definition for the docs generators. In an app with 77 features the descriptions drop from about 46.6k to 12.2k characters.

title: Agent manifest features and entities follow the role
detail: `buildAgentManifest` now leaves out a feature when none of its handlers, screens or navs remain in the manifest for the role, and an entity when no remaining handler or screen refers to it, no `get_`/`list_` tool of the role reads it and no reachable entity points at it through a reference field (one hop). Before, `features` and `entities` were identical for every role, so a restricted role paid for schemas it could not use in every system prompt. A translation-only feature such as `locale-de` no longer appears in `features`.

title: Local agent tool errors carry a code
detail: dispatchToolCall returns code invalid_tool_call for validation errors and unknown_tool for an unknown tool name, instead of a result without code. TOOL_CALL_ERROR_CODES names both.

title: dispatchToolCall documents which failures carry a code
detail: Only handler and dispatcher failures carry a code; local validation errors such as an unknown tool or bad arguments come back without one, and the JSDoc now says so.

title: Agent tool failures are classified instead of passing raw messages through
detail: dispatchToolCall now adds a code to failed tool results. Client errors keep their message, rate limits also set retryable and retryAfterSeconds. Server errors and unknown throws are logged with their cause and returned to the model as "Tool failed unexpectedly", so internal details such as database messages no longer reach the model. ToolCallRequest accepts an optional log.

title: buildToolCatalog throws when the manifest was built with denyQns the catalog options lack
migration: Pass the same denyQns list to buildAgentManifest and buildToolCatalog.

title: Agent manifest screen titles resolve per feature instead of by mount order
detail:
Agent manifest screen titles no longer depend on feature mount order
Two features with a screen of the same short id used to get the title of whichever feature was mounted first. The manifest now looks up the screen's own feature-prefixed title key first and falls back to the unprefixed key.

title: entity get/list tools honour agent.risk, PII-bearing system lists are high risk
detail: agent-tools: `get_<entity>` and `list_<entity>` take their risk from the entity handler's `agent.risk` instead of a hard-coded `low`. The SystemAdmin `user:list`, `user:detail` and `download-attempt:list` handlers declare `risk: "high"`.
migration: No action needed: handlers without an agent.risk hint stay low risk.

title: agent entity tools no longer filter on read-restricted fields
detail: agent-tools: `list_<entity>` filters and `find_<entity>_by_<field>` tools only offer filterable fields that every caller role may read without a row condition. A role- or ownership-restricted filterable field can no longer be probed through `totalCount` or hit/miss results.
migration: No action needed: fields whose access.read is not unconditionally open to the agent's roles drop out of list filters and find-by tools.

title: agent tool name collisions are disambiguated, audit search is substring, encrypted config bounds errors do not echo the value
detail: The agent manifest reports a detail screen's configured `idParam` and builds its label index once per manifest. Handler tools whose names collide after sanitizing or truncation are no longer dropped; the later one gets a QN-hash suffix. The audit log search matches event types by substring instead of exact equality. Config bounds errors no longer echo an encrypted value. The MFA account label never falls back to the internal user id. The tenant caps list resolves limits in parallel.

title: Manifest rejects unknown denyQns, drops navs under hidden parents; doc lint flags blank and exposed-undescribed handlers
detail: Agent tools: `buildAgentManifest` now throws when `denyQns` names a handler that is not registered, so a typo can no longer leave a handler exposed. Navs whose parent is hidden from the role are dropped from the manifest, and screens reachable only through them are no longer listed. The agent doc lint reports handlers that are exposed without a description and treats a blank description as a gap.
migration: `buildAgentManifest` now throws when `denyQns` names a handler that is not registered; remove stale or misspelled entries from your `denyQns` lists.

title: Agent doc lint reports exposed handlers with a non-convertible input schema
Agent manifest now resolves a screen's i18n-key description to English prose
detail:
buildAgentManifest passed screen.description straight through even when
a feature registered it as an i18n key (e.g. "audit.log.detail.subtitle")
rather than literal text, so agents saw the raw key instead of prose.
It now resolves through the registry's translations the same way
labelsForSuffix already does for entity/field labels, falling back to
the literal string when the description isn't a registered key.
